signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades under pressure as the yen dominates the G10 scorecard while the Canadian dollar laggards the peer group. Iran-Oman negotiations regarding the Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor and potential mine-clearing concessions are driving a sharp -5.39% drop in WTI oil to $76.0, directly undermining CAD's terms of trade. JPY 1W avg outperformance of +1.786% reflects a massive 2.794% spread over CAD's -1.008% decline, signaling a major thematic shift in the crosses. Despite a 125bp carry advantage for CAD/JPY, the 25d RR at -2.71 for EUR/JPY and -2.76 for USD/JPY confirms an aggressive institutional move into JPY protection. USD/JPY has already broken below its SMA200 at 157.97, confirming a structural shift in the yen's favor. Risk: Breakdown in Strait of Hormuz negotiations sparks a crude reversal and CAD recovery.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5889, holding firmly above its SMA200 (0.5827) and SMA20/50 cluster. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The real rate for NZD at -1.56% is the most accommodative in the G10, yet the market is pricing a hawkish shift with the RBNZ meeting on 2 September acting as a major catalyst. If data continues to beat, the crowded spec short faces an asymmetric squeeze risk toward 0.6000. Risk: RBNZ pivots to a hold stance or inflation expectations drop sharply, validating the current spec short.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility + Carry + Headline
signals.text: EUR/USD holds at 1.1525, supported by the SMA20 (1.1432) and SMA50 (1.1483) cluster as Hormuz reopening hopes dampen USD safe-haven appeal. The options market is pricing an elevated vol risk premium with ATM IV at 7.1% vs HV30 of 4.4%, a 2.7-point spread signaling high demand for protection above realized moves. This hedging activity occurs despite a +135bp carry advantage for the USD, as traders focus on the ECB's hawkish hike bias for the 10 September meeting. COT LF net short of -92,930 remains a headwind for the trend, but the combination of positive ESI and shifting geopolitical risk keeps the pair bid. Risk: Deterioration in US-Iran relations forces a return to USD safe-haven flows.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Sentiment Extreme
signals.text: USD/NOK retail sentiment has reached a total extreme at 100% long, positioning for a reversal as the pair trades at 9.537. This retail position directly fades the fundamental backdrop of a restrictive NOK real rate of +1.51% and a strong positive Economic Surprise Index (+34.4) for the krone. Technically, USD/NOK is positioned below its SMA20, 50, and 200, confirming a bearish trend that retail is unsuccessfully trying to catch. With the Norges Bank maintaining a hiking bias for its 13 August meeting, retail long capitulation is likely to accelerate the move lower. Risk: A significant miss in upcoming Norwegian inflation data allows Norges Bank to pivot to a hold, rescuing retail longs.
